newsitem.title: SPAIN: Radiotronica to post signficant '97 losses.
newsitem.headline: Radiotronica to post signficant '97 losses.

text.p: Spanish electronic equipment firm Radiotronica said on Friday it would post signficant losses in 1997 as a result of a number of economic problems which will force the firm to dismiss 652 workers.
In a statement to the stock market watchdog the CNMV, Radiotronica said its activities had been badly hit by a slump in trade and high costs.
Contracting in its lines and cables sector has fallen continuously since 1990, it said.

"Since 1990, trade with our main client has fallen continuously so that in 1997 it has been about 25 percent of what it was in 1990," the firm said. The main part of its workforce is dedicated to the lines and cables sector, it added.
The company said it expected turnover in the lines and cable division to be 3.0 billion pesetas in 1997 compared with a consolidated turnover of 16.0 billion pesetas.
In its telephony contract, Radiotronica said at expiry it had been informed that an open auction at free prices would be held which would render its costs non-competitive.

The remainder of the firm's activities, which are fundamentally subcontracted, have market prices similar to those in the lines and cables' division and therefore Radiotronica said it was not viable to dedicate the current workforce to these activities.

"In the current year the impact ... on results will be negative by an amount still undetermined, and will depend on the deals reached in negotiations with the trade unions which will start on July 7 and last a month," the firm said.
"In any case the losses in 1997 will be significant," it added.
The CNMV suspended trade in Radiotronica shares on Friday. Radiotronica said earlier on Friday it would dismiss 652 workers.
